what: Two bodies of missing Italians recovered from inside Maldives cave

clean_source_blocks.text: The bodies of two Italians who drowned in a scuba diving accident in the Maldives last week have been brought to the surface, local officials have told the BBC. "They were retrieved from the third chamber of the underwater cave by the specialist divers from Finland after a two-hour operation," Mohamed Hossain Shareef, a Maldivian government spokesperson told the BBC. The two bodies were being brought to the capital Male for identification. They were among five people who died in the accident. Two bodies remain inside. The first body of an Italian diver, who was a member of the group, was recovered shortly after Thursday's accident near Vaavu atoll. He has been named by Italian media as boat operations manager and diving instructor Gianluca Benedetti. Then on Saturday a Maldivian rescue diver died during a search for the bodies.
The two were among four divers located in the furthest chamber in the cave and their bodies were recovered by specialist divers.

In this handout photo release by Maldives President Media Division, a Finnish diver, left, gets ready to attempt to recover the bodies of two of the four Italians who died deep inside an underwater cave in an atoll earlier this month, at Alimathaa Island, in Vaavu Atoll, Maldives, Tuesday, May 19, 2026. Credit: AP/Uncredited MALE, Maldives — Finnish divers on Tuesday recovered the bodies of two of the four remaining Italians who died deep inside an underwater cave in an atoll in the Maldives, an official said. The bodies were located on Monday, when searches resumed after being suspended following the death of a local military diver during a perilous mission to try to reach them.

The bodies of two Italian divers were brought to the surface Tuesday after the Maldives' worst diving disaster, according to a government spokesman. The two were among five divers who failed to return after they went into the water on May 14, spokesman Mohamed Hussain Shareef said. Two more bodies are yet to be brought up from the same cave, at a depth of some 195 feet beneath the sea surface. The body of one member of the dive party was recovered Thursday, while a Maldivian rescuer died due to decompression complications on Saturday. Diving experts were planning to recover the remaining two bodies Wednesday. Italy's Foreign Ministry announced Monday that rescuers had located the bodies of the four Italian divers that were still deep inside the underwater cave in an atoll in the Maldives.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
The bodies of two Italians who drowned in a scuba diving accident in the Maldives last week have been brought to the surface, local officials have told the BBC.

"They were retrieved from the third chamber of the underwater cave by the specialist divers from Finland after a two-hour operation," Mohamed Hossain Shareef, a Maldivian government spokesperson told the BBC.

The two bodies were being brought to the capital Male for identification.

They were among five people who died in the accident. Two bodies remain inside.

The first body of an Italian diver, who was a member of the group, was recovered shortly after Thursday's accident near Vaavu atoll. He has been named by Italian media as boat operations manager and diving instructor Gianluca Benedetti.

Then on Saturday a Maldivian rescue diver died during a search for the bodies.

The four missing divers were eventually found by Finnish divers on Monday in the chamber of the cave furthest from the entrance. Known locally as "shark cave", it is up to 60m 197 ft) deep.

The mission to recover the remaining two bodies will resume on Wednesday and a Maldivian official was hopeful they would be retrieved the same day.

Finding the bodies will provide clues as to the cause of the accident. The recovery operation has been described as complex because of the depth of the cave and the lack of space and visibility. The entrance to the cave lies at a depth of 47m but the various chambers are at varyin depths.

The weather at the time of the dive on Thursday was described as rough and a  yellow warning had been issued for passenger boats and fishermen.

Four of the divers were part of a team from the University of Genoa, which told the BBC that it did not give approval for any kind of deep-sea dive as part of their scientific research.

"The requests submitted to the Maldivian authorities...were evidently made outside the scope of the mission authorised by the University," a spokesperson said.

A Maldivian government spokesperson told the BBC that the team had a permit to dive to a depth of 50m but had not mentioned the cave in their proposal.

Credit: AP/Uncredited

MALE, Maldives — Finnish divers on Tuesday recovered the bodies of two of the four remaining Italians who died deep inside an underwater cave in an atoll in the Maldives, an official said.

The bodies were located on Monday, when searches resumed after being suspended following the death of a local military diver during a perilous mission to try to reach them.

Five Italian divers went missing on Thursday, with one of the bodies recovered earlier. The plan is to recover the remaining two bodies on Wednesday.

The announcement that two bodies were recovered on Tuesday was made by presidential spokesperson Mohamed Hussain Shareef.

Maldives government spokesman Ahmed Shaam had earlier said that the three Finnish divers would retrieve the bodies, which were lying at a depth of around 60 meters (200 feet). The legal depth for recreational diving in the Maldives is 30 meters (nearly 100 feet).

payload.title: Suomalaiset sukeltajat nostivat kahden italialaissukeltajan ruumiit Malediiveilla
payload.summary: Kahden italialaissukeltajan ruumiit on saatu nostettua Malediiveilla vedenalaisesta luolasta. Turmassa kuoli yhteensä viisi ihmistä, ja kahden uhrin ruumiit ovat yhä luolassa.
payload.content:
Kahden Malediiveilla sukellusonnettomuudessa kuolleen italialaisen ruumiit on nostettu vedenalaisesta luolasta tiistaina. Paikallisten viranomaisten mukaan ruumiit saatiin esiin Vaavun atollin alueella sijaitsevan luolan kolmannesta kammiosta suomalaisista erikoissukeltajista koostuneen ryhmän noin kaksituntisen operaation jälkeen.

## Ruumiit nostettiin luolan syvimmästä osasta

Onnettomuudessa kuolleet italialaiset kuuluivat sukellusryhmään, joka ei palannut pintaan 14. toukokuuta tehdyn sukelluksen jälkeen. Viranomaisten mukaan kaksi nyt nostettua ruumista olivat osa neljän italialaisen ryhmää, joka oli paikannettu syvälle vedenalaiseen luolaan.

Ruumiit kuljetettiin Malediivien pääkaupunkiin Maléen tunnistamista varten. Luolassa on edelleen kahden uhrin ruumiit, joiden nostamista sukellusasiantuntijoiden oli lähdetietojen mukaan tarkoitus jatkaa keskiviikkona.

Yhden italialaissukeltajan ruumis saatiin nostettua jo pian torstain onnettomuuden jälkeen. Italialaismedioiden mukaan hän oli veneoperaatioista vastannut sukelluskouluttaja Gianluca Benedetti.

## Pelastustyö keskeytyi aiemmin kuolemantapauksen vuoksi

Etsintä- ja nostotyöt keskeytettiin aiemmin, kun malediivilainen pelastussukeltaja kuoli lauantaina operaation aikana. Hänen kerrottiin menehtyneen dekompressioon liittyneisiin komplikaatioihin. Ruumiit paikannettiin maanantaina, kun etsinnät jatkuivat tauon jälkeen.

Malediivien hallituksen edustaja Mohamed Hussain Shareef kertoi, että kaksi italialaissukeltajaa saatiin pintaan tiistaina. Onnettomuutta on kuvattu Malediivien vakavimmaksi sukellusonnettomuudeksi.

Luolan kerrottiin sijaitsevan noin 195 jalan eli noin 60 metrin syvyydessä merenpinnan alapuolella. Syvyys, suljettu luolaympäristö ja aiempi pelastussukeltajan kuolema kertovat operaation vaarallisuudesta. Viranomaiset eivät ole lähdeaineiston perusteella kertoneet tarkasti, mikä johti alkuperäiseen sukellusonnettomuuteen.
summary_bullets: Kahden italialaissukeltajan ruumiit nostettiin Malediiveilla vedenalaisesta luolasta.
Nostotyön tekivät suomalaiset erikoissukeltajat noin kaksituntisessa operaatiossa.
Onnettomuudessa kuoli yhteensä viisi ihmistä, ja kaksi ruumista on yhä luolassa.
payload.journalist_note: Juttu perustuu useisiin yhteneviin lähdetietoihin. Tarkkaa onnettomuuden syytä ei lähdeaineistossa vahvistettu, joten sitä ei arvioida artikkelissa.
